summary:
Set 107 Session 3 of 3, the terminal session: the acceptance walk, and it PASSED ON BOTH HALVES. The operator walked the new docs/tutorials/hello-world.md on a SECOND MACHINE -- their GHE-linked Windows account, not the machine that authored S1 or S2 -- on a fresh VS Code profile, with the PUBLISHED 0.47.0 from the Marketplace, driven by GitHub Copilot. Under 15 minutes in-window (Ctrl+Shift+P to 'HELLO, WORLD!' on screen), and four no's: no git command typed, no YAML edited, no host configured, no Dabbler setting changed. The set's only real acceptance test is answered.

TWO LIMITS ARE DISCLOSED ON THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND. The checklist Results were transcribed by the orchestrator from the operator's report, not filled in item by item during the walk, and every Result field says so. And the time is the OPERATOR'S ESTIMATE, NOT A STOPWATCH READING -- the walk was performed before the final checklist existed, so no clock mark was ever written down. Recorded as an estimate on purpose: a precise-looking number nobody measured is worse evidence than an honest approximate one, and discarding a real first run to get a cleaner instrument would have been worse still.

THE MOST USEFUL FINDING IS THE ONE THAT IS NOT IN THE NUMBER. The operator's dominant cost 'by far' was PREREQUISITE, not tutorial: getting VS Code running while logged into GitHub Enterprise the right way. Their organisation uses a special Windows account linked to a GHE account; what works is a PowerShell script launching VS Code under runas with a dedicated profile carrying GHE login settings -- reliable, but not seamless, with THREE separate logins remaining (runas, GHE, Copilot CLI). The spec excludes setup time precisely so it is not mistaken for tutorial complexity, and that exclusion earned its keep here: the sample is HOSTLESS and never contacts a host, so the GHE login is what makes COPILOT work, not what makes Dabbler work. TRIAGED, NOT FIXED -- host and identity onboarding is an explicit spec non-goal for hello-world.md, and adding it would rebuild the cognitive load this set exists to remove (removal-over-addition). Named as a follow-on set in s3-walk-evidence.md.

THE PUBLISHED BUILD WAS PROVEN WALK-VALID BEFORE THE WALK. 0.47.0's tag landed on 7f2f2f8 (S1's last commit), so what shipped is S1's tree; git diff vsix-v0.47.0..HEAD over the shipped extension touches exactly two consumer-bootstrap templates, neither on the walk path (the tutorial never scaffolds a repo). No new tag and no new publish were needed, and package.json is still 0.47.0 -- so 'just push a tag' would have meant cutting 0.48.0 for a link description, the release the operator had already declined.

THE OPERATOR RESIZED THE INSTRUMENT MID-SESSION, AND WAS RIGHT TO. The first checklist shipped nine items with a tutorial-quality interrogation bolted onto each; the verdict was 'daunting and tedious' -- UAT should confirm the most important things and let the human volunteer what annoyed them. Rebuilt to FOUR: human-facing text 15,149 -> 2,588 chars, preamble 4,777 -> 1,313, six clock marks -> two. The failure was one of ALTITUDE: items existed for reading the prerequisite list, for the extension install, and for a failure path the walker was explicitly told not to trigger. The standing UAT bar in project-guidance.md governs AMBIGUITY (name the exact button, quote the exact string) and the checklist still obeys it; what the bar lacked was a companion rule about VOLUME, proposed at Step 9.

THE CHECKLIST'S PROSE WAS ROUTED, ITS LITERALS WERE BOUND -- S2's discipline applied to the instrument that measures S2's work. That binding caught the routed draft twice, both times on product behaviour it could not have known: it promised 'a new VS Code window opens' (the command calls vscode.openFolder without forceNewWindow, so the CURRENT window reloads), and the builder's own first scoping pulled SAMPLE_STEP_PHRASE instead of SAMPLE_PROGRESS -- same keys, different strings, fragments of the RESUME sentence -- briefly quoting five stage labels no reader would ever see. Caught only because the builder PRINTS what it bound instead of trusting itself.

VERIFICATION: three phased rounds, and it found three real defects in this session's own work. Discovery fanned out 2/2 (both calls independently raised the same two), then the supplementary completeness pass added a third neither had seen; all three accepted, none disputed; remediation-review returned VERIFIED with 3 accepted / 0 rejected / 0 accepted-with-modification. (1) s3-checklist-builder.py hardcoded d:/Projects/... so the one artifact whose whole job is to be re-runnable was un-re-runnable by anyone else. (2) ai-assignment.md still argued for a six-mark timing protocol deriving four durations -- but the checklist was cut to two marks and the walk used none, so NONE of those durations exist; the design doc read as though they did, which is exactly the overclaim class this session's own conventions block named as material, sitting in the one file nobody re-read after the resize. Corrected rather than deleted, and propagated to every echo in one pass (L-065-1). (3) the transcription step had appended the walk's VERDICT into the checklist's Notes -- the walker's INSTRUCTIONS -- conflating the instrument with its own result; removed rather than reworded, since the outcome was already in the four Result fields and in s3-walk-evidence.md.

LAYER 3 CHARACTERISED, NOT EXCUSED. All 28 Playwright specs fail locally at Electron launch, before any assertion -- a residual known since S1. Four hypotheses tested and RULED OUT: the ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 this shell inherits from its VS Code extension host (real -- a bare Code.exe --version prints a NODE version -- but electronLaunch.ts's allowlist already defends against it, proven by a probe using that same scrubbed env), the resolved VS Code version, the sandboxed shell, and the Set 045 stale-bundle trap. Reduced past the test runner, playwright-core reports 'Process failed to launch!'. ONE HYPOTHESIS REMAINS, NAMED AS UNPROVEN: local Node 25.8.1 vs CI's pinned Node 20, unfalsifiable here for want of an nvm. CI ran Layer 3 green on this session's own commits across macos/ubuntu/windows, and this session changes no Explorer-rendering surface, no state writer and no fixture. A follow-on is owed because L-064-12's whole point is that a layer nobody can run locally rots silently.

SET-TERMINAL: change-log.md written; the advisory path-aware critique attempted via the first-party automated producer (ai_router.pull_critique) and blocked by provider rate limits on BOTH non-anthropic providers -- recorded as owed rather than fabricated, which the stage's own rule forbids; the gate is advisory and warns rather than blocks. No product code, no version bump, no publish: this session's touches are the tutorial's measurement, this set's artifacts, and its own tooling.
